JPM.rationale: JPMorgan Chase demonstrates strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 showed revenue of $49.84B (+10% YoY) and EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY), with sequential improvement across all key metrics. The Q2 2026 earnings call (July 22) revealed record results: net income of $16.9B, managed revenue of $58B (+27% YoY), investment banking fees +30%, and equity markets revenue +86%. The bank raised full-year NII guidance to ~$105.5B and announced a dividend increase to $1.65/share. ROE of 16.2% and net margin of 31.5% reflect excellent profitability. The balance sheet is massive ($4.9T assets) with $364B equity, and the bank maintains top global rankings in investment banking fees (8.4% market share), deposits, and payments. Valuation is moderate: P/E of 16.16x sits mid-range of its 13.7-17.8x 1-year range, while P/B of 2.615x is near the upper end of its 2.2-2.8x range. The stock has risen +11.8% over the past quarter to $349.90, suggesting the market has partially priced in the strong results. However, CEO Dimon's caution about sustainability of peak conditions (SpaceX IPO, exceptional trading) and warnings about economic headwinds temper enthusiasm. The near-term catalyst from the blowout Q2 earnings report is largely priced in given the stock's recent run. Macro backdrop shows rising Treasury yields (10Y at 4.71%) which support NII but also signal potential credit stress, while the yield curve has flattened ( T10Y2Y at 0.34%.
